BiblicalUsage: Ragliy is a footman, a foot soldier — the man who fights on foot. The Philistines slew thirty thousand footmen of Israel when the ark was taken; David took from Hadadezer a thousand chariots and seven hundred horsemen and twenty thousand footmen; and at Aphek, Israel slew of the Syrians a hundred thousand footmen in one day.
TheologicalSignificance: What I hear in this is that the footman is the forgotten soldier: no chariot, no horse, only his feet — and the battles of Israel were won and lost by such men.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
